questions.question: Which thinker argued that people possess natural rights to life, liberty, and property?
choices: Thomas Hobbes
John Locke
Niccolò Machiavelli
Jean-Baptiste Colbert

questions.question: Which thinker is especially associated with separation of governmental powers?
choices: Voltaire
Denis Diderot
Adam Smith
Montesquieu

questions.question: Which writer strongly defended religious toleration and freedom of expression?
choices: Voltaire
Louis XIV
Philip II
Metternich

questions.question: Who helped edit the Encyclopédie, a major Enlightenment reference work?
choices: Isaac Newton
Napoleon Bonaparte
Denis Diderot
Martin Luther

questions.question: What does social contract theory examine?
choices: The prices charged in overseas trade
The basis of political authority and obligations between people and government
The rules for hereditary noble marriages
The methods for constructing cathedral vaults

questions.question: Which writer argued for women's education and equality in A Vindication of the Rights of Woman?
choices: Mary Wollstonecraft
Olympe de Gouges
Mary Shelley
Jane Austen

questions.question: Which thinker is closely associated with the general will?
choices: John Locke
Montesquieu
Adam Smith
Jean-Jacques Rousseau

questions.question: How did Enlightenment thought challenge divine-right monarchy?
choices: It required every ruler to inherit unlimited power
It rejected all discussion of political institutions
It questioned whether birth and religion alone justified political authority
It made church approval the sole basis of government

questions.question: How did the Scientific Revolution influence Enlightenment thinkers?
choices: It encouraged applying reason and inquiry to social and political questions
It proved every existing political system was ideal
It ended interest in evidence and observation
It prevented scholars from questioning authority

questions.question: Why were salons and coffeehouses important?
choices: They served only as royal courts of law
They created spaces for discussing and circulating ideas
They replaced all printed publications
They excluded discussion of public questions by definition

questions.question: What did Locke argue about governments that violated natural rights?
choices: People must accept every ruler's actions permanently
Only foreign kings could judge their actions
Such governments automatically became democratic
People could have grounds to resist or replace them

questions.question: How did Hobbes's view differ from Locke's?
choices: Hobbes rejected government; Locke favored hereditary absolutism
Both required universal direct voting on every law
Hobbes emphasized strong authority to secure order; Locke stressed limited government protecting rights
Locke denied natural rights while Hobbes promoted them

questions.question: What was enlightened absolutism?
choices: Monarchs adopting selected reforms while retaining strong royal authority
The complete replacement of monarchies with republics
A system with no government or legal institutions
A policy prohibiting education outside royal households

questions.question: Why did printed works help spread Enlightenment ideas?
choices: They guaranteed that every reader agreed
They allowed arguments to circulate beyond face-to-face discussion
They prevented governments from practicing censorship
They eliminated differences in access to education

questions.question: Why is describing the Enlightenment as uniformly egalitarian inaccurate?
choices: Every thinker advocated identical political participation
All European societies ended slavery immediately
No writer questioned inherited privilege
Some thinkers endorsed rights while excluding women, enslaved people, or other groups

questions.question: A constitution assigns lawmaking, administration, and judging to separate institutions. Which idea influenced this design?
choices: Divine-right monarchy
Mercantilist trade regulation
Montesquieu's separation of powers
Hereditary social rank

questions.question: A ruler expands schooling but keeps final control over government. Which concept best fits?
choices: Enlightened absolutism
Direct democracy
Anarchism
Feudal decentralization

questions.question: Which argument most closely reflects Locke's political theory?
choices: Royal birth gives a ruler authority without limits
Government exists to protect rights and rests on consent
Religious uniformity is the sole purpose of government
Citizens lose all rights when government forms

questions.question: Which evidence would best reveal debate within the Enlightenment?
choices: Listing only the titles of royal palaces
Counting battles from the medieval Crusades
Mapping ancient irrigation systems
Comparing thinkers' differing views of authority, equality, and liberty

questions.question: Why did Enlightenment ideas matter to later revolutions?
choices: They prescribed one identical outcome for every revolution
They ended political disputes throughout Europe
They supplied arguments about rights, consent, and legitimate authority
They required every society to use the same constitution
